Jānuārius, Jānuāria, Jānuārium

adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis), declension

of January; January

Janus’s month (Varro, LL 6.34, rightly). Like every Roman month name it is an adjective: mēnse Jānuāriō, or Jānuāriō alone, “in January”; Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Jānuāriae, the 1st, 5th and 13th. Traupman gives the modern way of dating as well (p. 76).

Examples

  • quā rē Jānuāriō mēnse, ut cōnstituistī, cūrā ut Rōmae sīs

    so be sure to be in Rome in January, as you plannedCic. Att. 1.2.2

  • sed heus tū, diem meum scīs esse III Nōnās Jānuāriās; aderis igitur

    but listen: you know my birthday is the third day before the Nones of January, the 3rd; so you’ll be thereCic. Att. 13.42.3

  • Tertiō diē (mēnsis) Jānuāriī.

    On the third of January (the modern way; Traupman’s Cicero, giving his birthday).Traupman 76

  • mēnse Jānuāriō

    in JanuaryTraupman 335

See also month, the Kalends, New Year’s Day, December, February.
